title: A K Made of Pressures Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A doctor checks blood pressure, a cyclist checks tyre pressure and a cook watches the gauge on a gas cylinder. For gases, pressure is the easy number to measure. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Aarav reads his tyre gauge in bar and asks: can an equilibrium constant use pressures instead of concentrations?

You will see what homogeneous means (a smoothie, not a fruit salad), then watch nitrogen, hydrogen and ammonia molecules hit the walls of a tank on the molecule bench to build partial pressures that add up to the total. We write Kp for ammonia, derive Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn from pV = nRT step by step, count gas moles to find Δn, compare HI (Kp = Kc) with ammonia, and cover the units of K with R = 0.0831 bar L mol^-1 K^-1. Then a worked example, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 61 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
